I am 63 years old and have farmed these lands in Quzhou County for 40 years. With only my wife and me in the household, and both of us doing some off-farm work when we can, I have learned to manage my time carefully. I rely on the wheat-maize double cropping system for most of my 10.1 mu because it gives us grain security and a steady income, and I keep just a small plot of cotton because it pays well but demands too much labor for picking and spraying.

This year, I will put 9.6 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and leave 0.5 mu for cotton. For the winter wheat, I will rotary till before sowing in late October and use an improved wheat variety at 35 jin per mu. I will apply 50 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as a basal dressing, which gives me about 7.5 kg of nitrogen, 7.5 kg of phosphorus, and 7.5 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate four times from the well—overwintering, reviving green, jointing, and grain filling—because wheat needs steady water to reach good yield, and I expect about 1,000 kg per mu. I will spray insecticide three times, herbicide once, and fungicide twice to protect the crop.

Right after wheat harvest in early June, I will plant hybrid maize (Longping 318) using no-tillage to save time and labor during the busy summer rush. I will seed 1 package per mu and apply 40 kg per mu of 26-8-8 compound fertilizer as basal, giving roughly 10.4 kg nitrogen, 3.2 kg phosphorus, and 3.2 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate only once if the summer rains are decent—groundwater is getting costly and maize handles short dry spells better than wheat. I expect about 850 kg per mu. I will spray insecticide twice and herbicide once.

For the 0.5 mu of cotton, I will rotary till in spring and sow an improved variety at 2 jin per mu. I will apply 50 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as basal, and irrigate twice. Cotton pests are relentless here, so I will spray insecticide 12 times and herbicide once through the season. If the weather holds, I expect about 550 kg per mu of seed cotton.
